Display: The largest text: short, large words or numerals.
Use it rarely in an application: a hero figure, a first-run screen. It is set in the brand face.
Supply the text as children and a `size`: `large`, `medium` or `small`. `colorRole` states a colour where inheriting is wrong.
Headline: A page's or a section's heading.
Use one headline level per page section. It is set in the brand face.
Supply the text as children and a `size`: `large`, `medium` or `small`.
Title: A smaller heading: a card's title, a dialog's title, a list item's headline.
Use it for the heading of a contained thing. It is set in the brand face, at medium weight.
Supply the text as children and a `size`: `large`, `medium` or `small`.
Body: Use it for passages. Under a heading, give supporting text `colorRole="on-surface-variant"`. It is set in the plain face.
Supply the text as children and a `size`: `large`, `medium` or `small`.
Label: Short text inside or beside a control: a caption, a table head, a count.
Use it for words that label, not words that are read as a passage. It is set in the plain face, at medium weight.
Supply the text as children and a `size`: `large`, `medium` or `small`.

Pressable: A button, or with `href` a link, that holds anything: it gives its content the keyboard, a name, the state layer and the focus ring, and draws nothing else.
Use it around an avatar that opens a menu, a card pressed whole or a line of a transcript. Use `Button` or `IconButton` where the control is one of theirs.
The content as children, `onPress` or `href`, a name (`aria-label`) where the content has no text, and the shape as a class (`rounded-shape-full`).
Skeleton: A placeholder for content that is loading: a quiet block the size and shape of what will take its place, so the page does not jump when it arrives.
Use it while a first read is out, in the shape of what is coming. A `text` skeleton stands inside the type primitive it replaces and takes its line height.
Wrap the skeletons in a `SkeletonGroup` with a `label`, the line a screen reader hears. Give each a `shape` (`text`, `rectangle` or `circle`) and its size as a class.
Popover: A surface that opens beside the control that asked for it, holding a few controls or a short list; `PopoverTrigger` puts the control and the popover side by side.
Use it for filters, a short list of notifications or a small form that belongs to one control. Material 3 does not describe it; use a `Dialog` where the page must wait.
A pressable kit component and the `Popover` inside a `PopoverTrigger`. It opens on press, Enter or Space, and gives the focus back on close.
Tree: A hierarchy a person opens level by level: folders and files, sections and pages, categories.
Use it where rows have children. The arrow keys move between rows; Right opens a row and Left closes it.
A name (`aria-label`), and `TreeItem`s nested in each other, each an `id`, a `title` and an optional `icon`; `selectionMode` where rows are chosen.
Breadcrumbs: The path to the page a person is on: a row of links to each level above it, then the page itself, which is not a link.
Use it on a page deep enough that the way back is not one step. Put it in a `nav` with a name, so the path is a landmark.
One `Breadcrumb` a level, each with an `href` but the last.
ContextMenu: A menu asked for on something itself, where it is: the actions of a file, a row or a selection, opened by a right click, a long press or the Menu key.
Use it for actions that are also reachable another way: nothing on the page says a context menu is there.
The area as children, a name (`aria-label`) and `items`, the kit's `Menu` rows: each an `id`, a `label` and `onAction`, or a divider.
Link: A text link: a word or a phrase that goes somewhere, in a sentence or in a list of links.
Use it inside running text or as one of a list of links. It sets no type: it takes the size and weight of the text it sits in.
`href`, or `onPress` for a link that acts; `color` and `underline`; `target` for a link that leaves.
DropZone: An area files, or anything dragged, are dropped onto: from the computer, or from another part of the page.
Use it where a person adds files. Give it a button inside that picks files too: a drop is never the only way.
A name (`aria-label`), `onDrop`, and what the area says as children.
Button: The main way to act: a pill-shaped button in five colour styles and five sizes, round or square, as a button, a link or a toggle; and the floating action button.

Use `filled` for the one primary action of a screen, `tonal` for the next ones, `outlined` and `text` for the rest, and `elevated` where a button sits on a busy ground; `color="error"` for one that destroys. `size` runs from `xsmall` to `xlarge`, 32 to 136 pixels tall (`small` is the default), and `shape` is `round` or `square`. `isToggle` makes it a toggle whose corners turn when it is selected. The floating action button is the `fab` variant: one per screen, for its main action; with a label it is the extended FAB.

Supply the label as children and, where it helps, an `icon`: one of `Nemia.Icons`, or any component that takes a size and a class. An `href` makes it a link. A `fab` with no label takes an `aria-label`. `xsmall` and `small` answer over a 48 pixel target: leave that room around them.
IconButton: A button that shows an icon alone, as a button, a link or a toggle.

Use it for a compact action in a bar, a row or a card. Variants are `standard`, `filled` (the default), `tonal` and `outlined`, in five sizes from `xsmall` to `xlarge`. `isToggle` with `isSelected` makes it a toggle that shows whether it is on; `badge` sets a dot or a count on its icon.
Supply the `icon` (one of `Nemia.Icons`, or any component that takes a size and a class) and an `aria-label`: the icon is all a person sees, the label is all a screen reader says.
ButtonGroup: Buttons and icon buttons that answer to each other: a `standard` group that hugs them, or a `connected` row that selects.

Use `standard` for a few related actions side by side: a pressed button widens and its neighbours move. Use `connected` with a `selectionMode` (`single` or `multiple`) for a choice among a few options, in place of a segmented button. The group hands its `size` to its buttons.
Supply `Button`s or `IconButton`s as its direct children (a wrapped button loses its corners), a `variant` and a `size`; for a choice, `selectionMode`, and each child `isToggle` and an `id`.
FabMenu: A floating action button that opens two to six related actions above it, and turns into their close button.
Use it where the main action of a screen comes in a few kinds, such as a new note, photo or list. Place it at the window's trailing edge (`fixed bottom-4 end-4`): it grows upwards. Keep to six items.
Supply the FAB's `icon` and `aria-label`, the `items` (each an `id`, a `label`, an `icon` and an `onAction`), a `color` (`primary`, `secondary` or `tertiary`) and a `fabSize`.
SegmentedButton: Two to five options in one outlined row, for one choice or several.
Material no longer recommends it: for new work use a `ButtonGroup` with `variant="connected"` and a `selectionMode`. It is kept for screens that already use it.
Supply `Segment` children, each with an `id` and a label, or an icon and an `aria-label`; a `selectionMode` (`single`, the default, or `multiple`); and an `aria-label` that says what the row chooses.
SplitButton: A button for the main action, joined to a button that opens a menu of related ones.
Use it where one action is the usual one and a few others are its variants, such as Share and where to. It comes `elevated`, `filled` (the default), `tonal` or `outlined`, in the five button sizes.
Supply the leading button's label as children and its `onPress`, the menu's `items`, and `menuLabel`, the name of the button that opens the menu.
Avatar: A person's or a thing's picture, with a fallback when there is none.
Use it beside a name. Never as the only way to say who someone is.
Supply `src` and `alt`, and a `fallback` such as initials for when the picture is missing.
Badge: A notification dot, or a small count, on the corner of a destination's icon.

Use it on a navigation bar, a rail, a drawer, a tab or an icon button to say that something new waits there: the dot says there is something, a count says how many, up to 999+. Prefer the host's `badge` prop to a badge placed by hand: the host joins its words to the destination's name.

Supply the host's `badge` (a count, a short text, or `true` for the dot) and an optional `badgeLabel`. A badge alone takes a `value`, and `anchored` to sit on its positioned parent's corner. A count of 0 draws nothing.
Divider: A thin line between groups of content.
Use it to separate groups, not to box every row. It runs `horizontal` or `vertical`, and `full-width`, `inset` or `middle-inset`.
Supply nothing but its orientation and inset.
EmptyState: What a view shows when it has nothing to show.
Use it in place of an empty list or table: say what will appear here, and offer the action that fills it.
Supply a title, a `description`, optional `media`, and an `action` with at most one `secondaryAction`.
LoadingIndicator: A shape that morphs in a loop while something short loads.

Use it for a wait whose length is not known, between a fifth of a second and five seconds. `contained` sets it on a circle, for a loader over other content. Where the progress can be known, use a `ProgressIndicator` from the start.
Supply an `aria-label` that says what is loading, and a `size` from 24 to 240 pixels (48 by default).
Meter: A quantity within a known range, such as a quota, a disk's use or a score, as a bar.
Use it for a reading, not for a task under way: that is a `ProgressIndicator`. Give `color="error"` to a quantity over its limit, and say so in words: the colour never carries it alone.
Supply a `label` and a `value`, the range (`minValue`, `maxValue`) where it is not 0 to 100, `showValue` to print it, and `valueLabel` to say it in words ("3 of 5").
PreviewTrigger: A preview card that opens beside a link or an element on hover or focus.
Use it to show what a link leads to without leaving the page. Keep the card short: it closes when the pointer leaves.
Supply the trigger as the first child and a `PreviewCard` with the preview's content.
ProgressIndicator: Progress of something under way, drawn as a line or a circle.
Use `linear` across a container and `circular` in a small space. Leave the value out when the length of the wait is unknown.
Supply a `label`, and a value where one is known; `showValue` prints it.
Snackbar: A brief message at the foot of the screen, with one action at most.
Use it to confirm what just happened. It leaves by itself, so never put in it what a person must read or answer.
Supply a queue to one `SnackbarRegion` at the root of the app, and add messages to that queue.
Tag: A small label that marks a status or a category.

Use it for a state that is read, not pressed. Variants are `tonal`, `filled` and `outlined`, in `neutral`, `primary`, `secondary`, `tertiary` or `error`. Say the state in its words: the colour alone does not carry it.
Tooltip: A short hint shown on hover or keyboard focus: plain, or rich with a headline and supporting text.
Use a plain one to name an icon button, a rich one to explain a control. Never put in it what a person needs to act.
Wrap the control and the `Tooltip` in a `TooltipTrigger`. A rich one takes a `headline` and `supportingText`.
BottomSheet: A sheet anchored to the bottom of the screen, for supplementary content.

Use `standard` for content that goes with the page and leaves it usable, such as a player; `modal` for a short set of choices over a scrim, which must be dismissed. Its drag handle moves it between its heights, `partial` and `expanded`.
Supply `isOpen` with `onClose`, the content as children, and a `title` or an `aria-label`. A standard sheet sits at the bottom of its positioned container; `className="fixed"` pins it to the window.
Card: A container for one subject: a filled, outlined or elevated surface.
Use it to group what belongs to one thing. `filled` is the default; `outlined` on a ground of its own tone; `elevated` where the card must lift.
Supply a `CardContent` with a `headline`, `supportingText`, `media` and `actions`. `CardContent` takes those four and no children.
Carousel: A row of items, mostly pictures, that scrolls sideways.

Use `multi-browse` to show many items at once in three sizes, `hero` or `center-aligned-hero` to put one forward, `uncontained` for items of one width that run past the edge, and `full-screen` for one item at a time. On a page that scrolls down, give a Show all button or an arrow beside its header: the carousel does not.
Supply `CarouselItem` children, each with its picture and an `onPress` or an `href`, a `layout`, and an `aria-label` for the row.
Dialog: A dialog: a title, supporting text and its actions, drawn in place or, as `ModalDialog`, over the page.
Use it for a decision or a short task that must be finished or dismissed before going on. Give a confirmation that must be answered `role="alertdialog"`: a click outside then no longer dismisses it.

Supply a `title`, `supportingText` or children, and `actions`: the labels of a confirm and a cancel, or buttons of your own. `ModalDialog` takes the same, with `isOpen` and `onClose`, and comes `basic` or `fullscreen`.
DialogContent: The body a dialog draws: an optional icon, a title, supporting text and its actions.
Use it where a dialog's layout is wanted in a container of your own. `Dialog` already draws it.
Supply a `title`, `supportingText` or children, and `actions`: the labels of a confirm and a cancel, or buttons of your own.
Disclosure: A heading that opens and closes the content under it; several in a group make an accordion.
Use it for content most people skip. Do not hide in it what a person needs to decide.
Supply a `DisclosureHeader` with a `DisclosureTrigger`, and a `DisclosurePanel`. A `DisclosureGroup` holds several.
GridList: A list or a grid of items a person can move through, select and act on.
Use it for a list the keyboard walks through row by row. Use a `Table` when rows are compared by column.
Supply `GridListItem` children, each with a `ListItem` or a `Card` inside, and an `aria-label` for the list.
ListItem: One row of a list: a headline, supporting text, and an element at each end.
Use it for every row of a list, a menu-like panel or a settings page, so rows line up.
Supply a `headline`, optional `supportingText`, and a `leadingElement` and `trailingElement`: an icon, an avatar, a switch, a tag.
Modal: The veil and the centred layer that content opens in, over the page.
Use it to open content of your own over the page. For a dialog, `ModalDialog` already includes it. One modal at a time.
Supply the content as children, and `isOpen` with `onOpenChange`.
SideSheet: A panel that slides in from an edge for secondary content.
Use it for detail or filters that go with the page behind it. It opens from the `right` or the `left`.
Supply a `title`, the content as children, an optional `footer`, and `isOpen` with `onClose`.
Table: A data table whose columns can sort.
Use it where rows are compared by column. Align numbers to the `end`.
Supply a `TableHeader` of `Column`s and a `TableBody` of `Row`s of `Cell`s, and an `aria-label`.
Tabs: Views of one subject, one shown at a time.
Use `primary` tabs for the main views of a page and `secondary` tabs inside one of them. Not for steps of a flow.
Supply a `TabList` of `Tab`s and a `TabPanel` for each. A `Tab` takes an `icon`, above or beside its label.
BottomNavigation: Three to five destinations at the foot of a small screen.
Use it on a phone. On a wider screen use a `NavigationRail` or a `NavigationDrawer`.
Supply `items`, each with a label and an icon, and the selected key.
Menu: A list of choices that opens from a button.
Use it for the actions of one thing, or the overflow of a bar. Not for navigation between pages.
MenuItem: Use it inside a `Menu`, or to draw a row that looks like one.
Supply a `label`, and where they help a `leadingIcon`, a `trailingIcon`, `supportingText` or a `shortcut`.
NavigationDrawer: A side panel of destinations, standing beside the page or opening over it.
Use `standard` on a wide screen and `modal` on a narrow one.
Supply `items` or `sections` of them, an optional `headline`, and the selected key.
NavigationRail: Destinations down the side of a medium or wide screen.
Use it for three to seven destinations of equal weight. It can expand to show its labels.
Supply `items`, each with a label and an icon, the selected key, and an optional `header` and `footer`.
SearchBar: A search bar, and the search view it opens, where suggestions and results are listed as a person types.

Use `SearchBar` for a field that runs its query on Enter. Use `SearchView` where suggestions or results should list as one types: `docked` opens over the bar, `full-screen` fills the window, each `divided` or `contained`. In a `TopAppBar`, `search` takes the title's place.
Supply a `placeholder`, which is also its name; `leading` and `trailing` icon buttons or an avatar; and for a view, `SearchViewItem`s in `SearchViewSection`s, with `onAction` or `onSubmit`.
Toolbar: A row of the actions that belong to the current page, docked to the bottom of the window or floating over the content.

Use `docked` across the bottom of a window, in place of a bottom app bar, and `floating` over the content; `vibrant` draws the eye where `standard` does not. `fab` sets a floating action button beside a floating toolbar. Give it an `aria-label` where a page has more than one.
Supply standard `IconButton`s and text `Button`s as children, which the toolbar colours; a `variant`, a `color`, an `orientation`, and an optional `fab`.
TopAppBar: The bar at the top of a screen: its title, a way back or to the menu, and its actions.
Use one per screen. It comes `small`, `center-aligned`, `medium` or `large`.
Supply the `title`, a navigation icon button, and the actions as icon buttons.
Checkbox: A box for a choice that is on or off; grouped, for several of a set.
Use it where a person picks any number of options, or accepts one thing. For a setting that takes effect at once, use a `Switch`.
Supply the label as children. A `CheckboxGroup` takes a `label`, `supportingText` and an `errorMessage`.
Chip: A compact element that filters, suggests an action or holds an entry.
Use `assist` for a suggested action, `filter` for a choice that narrows what is shown, `input` for an entry a person made. A `ChipGroup` holds a set.
Supply the label as children; a `ChipGroup` takes a `label`.
ColorPicker: A colour chosen by area, slider, field or swatch.
Use it where a person picks a colour freely. Offer swatches where the choice is among a few.
Supply a `label`, and the parts to show as children: `ColorArea`, `ColorSlider`, `ColorField`, `ColorSwatch`.
DatePicker: A date field whose calendar button opens a calendar, for one date (`DatePicker`) or a range (`DateRangePicker`).

Use `docked` (the default) on a wide screen, `modal` where the calendar should hold the focus, and `fullscreen` on a compact window. A person may also type the date in the field. A range picker is always full screen.

Supply a `label` and an `@internationalized/date` value (`Nemia.Dates.parseDate("2026-06-15")`), and where they apply `minValue`, `maxValue` and `isDateUnavailable`. Set the locale with `Nemia.Aria.I18nProvider`.
Radio: Use it for two to five options that exclude each other and should all be seen. For more, use a `Select`.
Supply `Radio` children with their labels to a `RadioGroup`, which takes a `label`, `supportingText` and an `errorMessage`.
Select: One choice from a list that opens from a field.
Use it for more options than radios show well. Where a person would rather type, use a `ComboBox`.
Supply a `label` and `SelectItem` children, each with a `label` and optional `supportingText` and icons.
Slider: A value, or a range, picked along a track.
Use it where the feel of the value matters more than its exact number. Offer a `NumberField` beside it where the number matters.
Supply a label, the range, and `showOutput` to print the value.
Switch: A toggle for a setting that takes effect at once.
Use it for on or off with no confirm step. In a form that is sent later, use a `Checkbox`.
Supply the label as children. `icons` draws a mark in the thumb.
TimePicker: A field that opens a dialog to pick an hour and a minute, on a clock dial or typed.
Use it for a time of day. The dial suits a pointer and the typed input a keyboard; a person can switch between them. `hourCycle` sets 12 or 24 hours, else the locale does.
Supply a `label` and a `Time` value (`new Nemia.Dates.Time(7, 0)`), and where it helps a `defaultMode` (`dial` or `input`) and an `orientation`.
ComboBox: A field that filters a list as a person types, for one choice or several.
Use it for a long list. With `multiple`, each choice becomes a chip in the field.
Supply a `label` and `ComboBoxItem` children, and optional `supportingText` and `errorMessage`.
ImageField: A field that takes one image, dropped or chosen, and shows it.
Use it for a single picture in a form. It refuses a file of the wrong type or over the size given, and says which.
Supply a `label`, the accepted types and largest size, and the words of its buttons.
NumberField: A field for a number, with steppers.
Use it for a quantity a person may type or nudge.
Supply a `label`, and the range and step where there are any.
PhoneField: A field for a phone number, with a country to pick.
Use it wherever a phone number is asked: it formats as the country writes it.
Supply a `label` and, where known, the default country.
TextField: A field for a line or more of text.
Use `outlined` on a busy ground and `filled` on a plain one; keep to one in a form. Put the hint in `supportingText`, never in a placeholder alone.
Supply a `label`, and where they help `supportingText`, an `errorMessage` and icons.
